motion.name: ease-out
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)
motion.purpose: Default CSS easing for every state change.

motion.name: ease-in
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)

motion.name: button-press
motion.value: 160ms ease-out; active translateY(1px) scale(0.98)

motion.name: button-colour
motion.value: 200ms ease-out

motion.name: badge-flip
motion.value: 760ms ease-out rotateY(180deg), perspective 1400px; focus moves after 380ms

motion.name: sticker-peel
motion.value: 420ms ease-out; rotate(rot*0.3) translateY(-8px) scale(1.04); others opacity .38 saturate(.6) 300ms
motion.purpose: Hero sticker peek; its float is paused while peeled or focus-visible.

motion.name: sticker-caption
motion.value: opacity 220ms, transform 320ms ease-out, 6px slide; cap-top (s-a, s-c, s-d) opens above: bottom calc(100% + 14px), slides down from 6px
motion.purpose: Caption pill in/out on hover or focus only; no caption shows at rest.

motion.name: sticker-float
motion.value: @keyframes float alternate infinite ease-in-out on the inner span.float: translate3d(-x,-y,0) rotate(-r) to translate3d(x,y,0) rotate(r); vars --float-t (7s), --float-d (negative), --float-y (9px), --float-r (1.2deg), --float-x (4px); s-a 7.4s/-1.2s/9px/1deg, s-b 6.2s/-3.4s/11px/1.6deg/x3, s-c 8.6s/-5.1s/8px/0.8deg/x6, s-d 6.9s/-2.3s/10px/1.3deg, seal 5.6s/-0.6s/6px/2.4deg/x2; none under reduced motion
motion.purpose: Idle drift of each hero sticker, out of step.

motion.name: sticker-parallax
motion.value: fine pointer only; pointer across the VIEWPORT (not the hero) -1..1, viewport size read on resize, not per move; target 16px*depth x, 11px*depth y; ease 0.08 per tick; depth s-a 1.3, s-b 0.7, s-c 1, s-d 0.55, seal 1.6; written as --px/--py and applied via the individual translate property on li.slot-li (never transform, which GSAP owns for the entrance); starts only when the entrance timeline completes, since GSAP writes translate: none on the slots while their from() runs, so translate and transform never fight; ticker removes itself at rest; hero pointerleave eases home, and at rest at home the inline --px/--py are dropped
motion.purpose: Stickers lean toward the cursor by depth.

motion.name: hero-dust
motion.value: canvas.hero-dust inset 0, z 1, aria-hidden; specks count min(300, (w+300)*(h+180)/7200); depth z 0.15..1, radius 0.6+1.5z, alpha 0.18+0.42z, wander up to 3px/s; 12% chads 6.4x2px r1 spinning; inks 242,242,238 (x2), 229,228,223, chad 201,204,214; lean 150px*z x and 90px*z y toward the pointer, eased 2.2/s; frame loop dt cap 50ms, no frames while hero off screen or tab hidden; dpr cap 2; hero page box cached with its size and compared with the pointer's page position, so no pointer move forces a layout; chads use roundRect, or rect where it is missing (Firefox before 112, Safari before 16); guarded: a throw leaves the canvas empty and the rest of the home motion runs on; reduced motion: one still draw, redrawn on resize
motion.purpose: Field of punched dust behind the hero type and stickers.

motion.name: icon-sticker-wave
motion.value: .closing:hover .ico-stk.is-wave: 1.2s ease-out once, transform-origin 70% 90%, rotate 14deg/-8deg/10deg/-3deg at 20/40/60/80%
motion.purpose: Closing wave rocks from the wrist on panel hover.

motion.name: print-straighten
motion.value: 600ms ease-out; rotate(0) translateY(-6px)
motion.purpose: Screenshot print on project card hover.

motion.name: nav
motion.value: hide translateY(-100%) 380ms; solid bg 300ms; underline 260ms; solid after 40px; hide when scrolling down past 0.8vh

motion.name: agenda-row
motion.value: row opacity 260ms to .4; title translateX clamp(12px,2vw,32px) 520ms

motion.name: lenis
motion.value: lerp 0.11, wheelMultiplier 0.95; anchor scrollTo offset -24, duration 1.1

motion.name: pendulum
motion.value: acc = -36*a - 2.4*v; dt cap 40ms; sleep |a|<0.02 and |v|<0.05; drag clamp +/-38deg; velocity smoothing 0.6/0.4; release cap 260deg/s; click = <6px travel and <350ms; flip kick +/-34; entrance kick 58; scroll tug velocity*0.9 clamped +/-6 while hero visible

motion.name: entrance
motion.value: delay .12, defaults expo.out: nav opacity 0.6s@0; pendulum from y -95vh 0.78s power3.in @0.05 then kick 58; stickers from opacity 0 scale 1.22 rot 9, 0.5s back.out(1.5) stagger .075 @0.62; lede lines yPercent 108 0.9s stagger .09 @0.78; hero buttons y 14 opacity 0 0.6s stagger .07 @1.0; its onComplete starts the sticker lean

motion.name: chip-slap
motion.value: from opacity 0 scale 1.3 rotation +=10, 0.45s back.out(1.6), stagger .045, once at top 82%

motion.name: leader-draw
motion.value: once at top 72%: dot scale 0>1 0.35s back.out(2); path dashoffset 1>0 0.8s power2.inOut @0.05; pin from y10 scale .96 opacity 0, 0.55s expo.out @0.62

motion.name: reel-drift
motion.value: track translateX 0 to -50% (two copies, second aria-hidden) linear infinite; duration = half track width / 38px per s; hover on a fine pointer eases playbackRate to 0.25 over 0.8s power2.out (back to 1 on leave); paused for :focus-within (the reel itself is tabindex 0, role region) and when off screen (IntersectionObserver); no pause button; hover on a pass straightens it to 30% of its tilt and lifts 6px, 420ms expo.out
motion.purpose: Achievements reel (slows on hover, stops on focus and off screen).

motion.name: ach-photo-turn
motion.value: up to 4 photos per pass stacked in one 4:3 frame; opacity 900ms ease-out and scale 1.04 to 1 over 1600ms; one turn every 3600ms, first at 1200ms + 750ms*pass index; pass and clone together; skipped while the reel has focus within (its keyboard stop), is off screen, or the tab is hidden; dots: 6px, active 14px stock, 320ms; none under reduced motion (first photo, dots hidden)

motion.name: agenda-preview
motion.value: quickTo x/y 0.55s power3, offset +28px x; show 0.4s expo.out random rot -4..4; hide 0.25s power2.in to scale .85; every pointer entry (a row entered from outside the agenda, or a row arriving under a still cursor while scrolling) restarts both quickTo tweens at the cursor, passing x = pointer+28, y = pointer - half height as start and end, so the next move resumes from there (a plain set would hold only until the next move); row to row inside the agenda it keeps trailing; keyboard focus aims it at the row (min(row right - width - 180, viewport - width - 24), centred on the row), never at a stale pointer
motion.purpose: Cursor-trailing activity photo; restarts at the cursor on every pointer entry.

motion.name: cord-draw
motion.value: scaleY 0>1 scrub 0.4 from #about top-bottom to #contact bottom-bottom; fade-in 400ms; hidden under 860px

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no Lenis, no pendulum, no entrance; transitions 1ms; flip becomes 180ms linear opacity cross-fade; cord full; leaders drawn; dust drawn once and still; stickers do not float or lean; reel stands still as a keyboard-scrollable snap row (label "Achievements, scroll sideways") showing each pass's first photo, dots hidden; preview duration 0

motion.name: case-scroll-spy
motion.value: current = last .cs-page whose top <= 0.35 * innerHeight (else the first); on scroll + resize, one rAF per frame; no IntersectionObserver
motion.purpose: Program index current row; under 860px the row (not the page) scrolls to centre the active pill, smooth or instant under reduced motion.

motion.name: case-cord-progress
motion.value: cord-fill scaleY 0>1, linear both, animation-timeline: scroll(root block); fallback and reduced motion scaleY(1)
motion.purpose: Cord as reading progress on the case study, no script.

motion.name: arch-wire-draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset length>0, 700ms cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), stagger 90ms in flow order; once at 35% of the field visible
motion.purpose: Architecture cords drawing in; reduced motion: drawn, no transition.

motion.name: demo-autoplay
motion.value: muted loop playsinline; play at 50% visible unless user paused; pause when out of view; never under reduced motion

motion.name: demo-toggle
motion.value: press scale .96 (idle pill .98), 160ms ease-out; background 200ms

motion.name: next-card-hover
motion.value: translateY(-4px) + lift shadow, 420ms ease-out

motion.name: case-anchor-scroll
motion.value: CSS scroll-behavior: smooth, scroll-padding-top 104px (132px under 860px); auto under reduced motion
motion.purpose: Case study anchor jumps; no Lenis on this page.

breakpoints.name: wide-hero-tune
breakpoints.purpose: Statement block is 60vw wide; the seal drops below the action row, under Download CV (left gutter + 250px, top 13% + 4.16 lede-fs + 104px).

materials.name: twill

narrative.overview:
Recruiters meet this engineer the way they meet candidates at a career fair: by reading the badge. The page is sewn from two woven lanyard colourways, navy and concrete, panel to panel, with a stitched seam at every join; everything readable is printed on off-white PVC badge stock in near-black ink, hung from silver clip metal. Project screenshots are die-cut stickers with white kiss-cut borders slapped onto the webbing; metrics hang off them on die-cut tags tied with leader lines; achievements are photo passes hanging from a navy strap that rides slowly past, rank told by the cut of a tag; activities are the event agenda; experience is the itinerary. One vertical cord runs down the left of the page and every section clips onto it.

The system is physical, not digital. Depth comes from objects lying on fabric (neutral dark drop shadows under hung or stuck things), never from glow, gloss, or a metallic sheen. State is told by form (a tag's cut, a sticker lifting) and printed words, never by hue alone. The only saturated surfaces are the two webbings themselves; content never gets its own accent colour. One type family, Archivo variable, does everything by moving along its width axis: expanded black for names and display, normal width for reading, condensed caps for printed labels.

This file is derived from the shipped mockup (`mockup/index.html`, `mockup/styles.css`, `mockup/main.js`, `mockup/cv.html`). It is the spec for the production build (Next.js + SQLite, public `/`, `/projects/[slug]`, `/cv`, plus `/admin`). The owner's name, portrait, and GitHub account are real; every other name, metric, screenshot, and achievement in the mockup is synthetic and must be replaced (see the content checklist in Do's and Don'ts).

The two-colourway world replaced the original single ultramarine ground on 2026-11-14 at the owner's request (the ultramarine read as too loud). The home page and the CV carry the revision. The case study page has not been migrated yet (see below).
keyCharacteristics: Two woven webbing colourways, navy and concrete, alternating section by section with the raster twill on every panel and a stitched seam at every join.
Content on off-white badge stock in near-black ink; 18px card corners, 16px sticker corners, full pills for buttons.
One family, Archivo variable (wdth 62 to 125, wght 100 to 900), roles separated by width as much as weight.

Physical motion: a damped pendulum badge on a concrete strap with a metal ring and lobster clasp, stickers that slap down and then drift and lean with the pointer over a field of punched dust, leader lines that draw to the result.
State by form and printed word, never by colour alone.
Every creative moment has a plain readable path; reduced motion renders every section in its final state.
Case studies read as an event program: a sticky index with a printed 'Reading' tag, one stock page per section, the cord as reading progress.

rules.name: The Two Colourway Rule
rules.body: The page is sewn from two webbings and nothing else: navy and concrete alternate panel by panel in story order (hero navy, about concrete, work navy, achievements concrete, activities navy, experience concrete, closing navy), every join carries the stitched seam, and a panel never changes colourway partway through. Webbing colours are grounds, straps, and printed bands; they never become a text highlight on stock. On stock and paper navy appears only as print: the badge's header band, the CV's strap, cord, tabs, rule, and metric figures.

rules.name: The State By Form Rule
rules.body: Rank, role, and status are told by cut, length, and the printed word. Two items that differ only by hue are a defect.

rules.name: The Press Palette Rule
rules.body: Two webbings, stock, white, ink, flat metal. A new colour needs a physical reason (it is a material on a badge or lanyard), or it does not ship. The live green dot is the one standing exception.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy moves on `wdth` as much as on weight: names and display at 118 to 125, reading at 96 to 100, printed labels at 72 to 85. Never fake width with `transform: scaleX` or letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any figure the eye compares (metrics, years, dates, GPA, latency) sets `font-feature-settings: "tnum" 1`.

rules.name: The Printed Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked condensed caps exist only as print on a physical object (rank tag, role tag, itinerary list label, strap, seal, the badge's header band, and on the CV the section tabs, cut tags, and dates). They never float above a heading as a section label.

rules.name: The Neutral Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is near-black and offset down. A shadow tinted with the ground, the field colour, or white is a glow and is banned.

rules.name: The Hole Not Light Rule
rules.body: Insets are only for things cut into material (slots, eyelets, webbing edges). Never use an inset as a highlight or rim light.

rules.name: The Code Is Data Rule
rules.body: Identifiers in prose stay in Archivo at 700, wdth 85, on a 7% ink wash with label-cut corners. Monospace never appears, not even for code.

dos: - **Do** put the weave on each section panel: the panel's ground colour plus `assets/textures/twill.png` at 24px, and on concrete panels a flat 55% concrete layer over the tile (written as a single-colour `linear-gradient`, which is a flat tint, not a gradient). Alternate navy and concrete in story order and sew every join with the seam.

- **Do** produce woven materials as raster tiles from `mockup/assets-src/make_textures.py`: a 48px 2/2 twill (white thread highlight and deep `rgb(4,6,30)` shade as alpha over the ground, displayed at 24px) and a 32px ribbed webbing (displayed at 16px over concrete for the strap, its tab, and the cord fill, and over navy for the reel strap and each pass's short strap). Regenerate rather than hand-draw or approximate with CSS gradients.

- **Do** draw the strap hardware as flat SVG facets from the four metal tokens, with the ring's top bar hidden inside the tab's fold and the clasp hooked through the badge slot (front strand over the card, back strand hidden behind it).
- **Do** make seals and medals as flat one-ink discs with a stock ring; none is metallic.
- **Do** tell state by form: tag cut for rank and role, sticker lift for focus, printed word always present.

- **Do** use real raster screenshots of the actual product for stickers and prints (PNG, at least 1440x900 for desktop, 780x1688 for phone), cropped from the top-left, with honest alt text describing what the screen shows.
- **Do** give every project one real metric on its pin, with what it measures in plain words.
- **Do** set every comparable figure with tabular numbers.

- **Do** keep every interaction keyboard reachable with a visible 3px focus ring (offset 3px, radius 6px) in the on-ground colour of its panel (stock on navy, ink on concrete), and ink on stock surfaces. Stock cards (project cards, the itinerary) keep an ink ring on either colourway.

- **Do** use these motion constants: Lenis `lerp: 0.11, wheelMultiplier: 0.95`; pendulum `K = 36, C = 2.4` integrated per GSAP tick (dt capped at 40ms, sleeps when `|a| < 0.02` and `|v| < 0.05`), drag clamped to +/-38deg with velocity smoothed 0.6/0.4 and capped at 260deg/s on release, scroll velocity tugging the strap (`velocity * 0.9`, clamped +/-6) only while the hero is visible.

- **Do** run the one authored entrance exactly once, defaults `expo.out`, after 0.12s: nav fades in (0.6s, at 0); the pendulum drops from -95vh (0.78s `power3.in`, at 0.05s) then kicks the spring by 58deg/s; stickers slap down from `scale 1.22, rotation 9, opacity 0` (0.5s `back.out(1.5)`, stagger 0.075s, at 0.62s); lede lines rise from `yPercent 108` (0.9s, stagger 0.09s, at 0.78s); hero buttons rise 14px (0.6s, stagger 0.07s, at 1.0s).
- **Do** slap the stack chips on once at 82% viewport (from `scale 1.3, rotation +=10, opacity 0`, 0.45s `back.out(1.6)`, stagger 0.045s).
- **Do** use the two CSS easings for state changes: `ease-out` `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and `ease-in` `cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0)`.

- **Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` with the final state: no Lenis, no pendulum ticker, no entrance, no chip slap, leader lines and pins already drawn, cord fully drawn, the achievements reel standing still as a snap row, preview following with zero duration, CSS transitions at 1ms, and the badge flip replaced by a 180ms opacity cross-fade between faces with no 3D rotation.
- **Do** keep the page fully readable with scripts off: GSAP absent means the badge, stickers, cards, the achievements reel (without its second copy), and agenda all render static.
- **Do** measure and fit the first name to the badge width in production (Next.js), stepping size or `wdth` down until it fits.

- **Do** keep the owner's real details as they are: the name (Muhammad Jafar Fadli; the badge prints "Jafar" over "Fadli", the nav brand and strap read "Jafar Fadli"), the portrait (`mockup/assets/photos/owner-badge.jpg` and `owner-cutout.png`, provenance in `SOURCES.txt`), and the GitHub account `github.com/jafarfadli`.

- **Do** replace the deliberate placeholders before launch: the email `hello@jafarfadli.example`, the domain `jafarfadli.example` (badge header band, CV contact list), and the LinkedIn URL `linkedin.example/in/jafarfadli` and its empty `#` link in the closing.

- **Do** replace all remaining synthetic content before launch: the role, stack, location, and availability lines (confirm them with the owner); the four projects (Ledgerly, Rute, Kanbo, Pantau) with their copy, metrics, tags, and per-project field colours; `mockup/assets/screens/*.png` (generated mock screens); `mockup/assets/photos/act-*.jpg` (Unsplash stand-ins listed in `SOURCES.txt`); the achievement photos, which are temporary reuses of activity photos (act-stage, act-mentor, act-hackathon, act-workshop, act-conf) until the owner supplies real ones or approves dedicated placeholders; `mockup/assets/qr-cv.svg` (must encode the real `/cv` URL, stock background); the five achievements, six activities, three experience stops, education, GPA, and the CV text; remove the "Mockup with sample content" note and every "(sample)" marker.
- **Do** keep provenance for every shipping raster (source or generator next to the asset).
- **Do** print a result's before value as a legible line ("from 13.1 days") above the value, in `clip-metal` on the ink tag.
- **Do** describe every architecture cord in the flows list under the diagram, in drawing order, and draw the cords from that list and the booth placements; never hand-draw connector paths.
- **Do** drive the program index from scroll position (35% of the viewport, rAF-throttled), not IntersectionObserver.
- **Do** render Live site and Code only when the project record has those URLs.
- **Do** end a case study's pages with "What I'd do next" (index label "Next steps"), followed by the Next project section on the ground.
- **Do** use a mid-flow frame of the demo recording as its poster, and keep its provenance next to the video.
- **Do** autoplay a demo only muted, looping, while at least half visible, and with motion allowed; pause it when it leaves view and let a user pause stick.
- **Do** draw lines (architecture cords) with `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`, the CSS twin of the leader lines' `power2.inOut`.

- **Do** keep the achievements photos turning in step and out of step: 3600ms per pass, first turn at 1200ms plus 750ms per pass, pass and clone together, and none while the reel has focus, is off screen, or the tab is hidden.
donts: - **Don't** put eyebrow or kicker labels (small uppercase tracked text) above section headings or titles; printed labels live only on physical objects (rank tags, role tags, strap, seals, itinerary list labels).

- **Don't** use gradient text, gradient fills, conic or holographic gradients, or a fake metallic or foil sheen on any surface, seal, tag, or clip. The only gradients are the shades named under Fold and hole shading and the mask that fades phone strap tops.
- **Don't** use glow, tinted halos, or coloured shadows; shadows are neutral near-black and offset down.

- **Don't** introduce an accent colour or give roles or ranks their own hue; sections differ only by the two webbing colourways in fixed alternation, and everything else by cut, length, and the printed word.
- **Don't** fake screenshots with styled divs or CSS mock UIs; use real raster screenshots.
- **Don't** use monospace type as costume (no terminal prompts, no code-styled labels); there is no monospace in the system.

- **Don't** add a marquee or ticker beyond the achievements reel. That reel is the one marquee, built because the owner asked for the motion (reference: danielsun.space); it slows to a quarter speed on hover, stops for keyboard focus on the strip itself and when off screen, and stands still under reduced motion. It has no pause button (owner decision 2026-11-14); do not add round controls to it. A second moving strip is refused.
- **Don't** use em dashes in copy; use commas, colons, or full stops.
- **Don't** present synthetic or estimated metrics as real; a metric without a source does not ship.
- **Don't** add a second type family or swap Archivo for a system display face.
- **Don't** add a third colourway, a theme toggle, a dark-mode inversion, or a gradient between panels; navy and concrete are the whole set, and a join is always a stitched seam.
- **Don't** give the strap, cord, or hardware their own per-panel colour; they are one material that crosses both colourways.
- **Don't** render any copy in canvas, WebGL, or images; all text is DOM text.
- **Don't** add hero stickers beyond the five slots or let them cross into the lanyard's half of the hero; the badge hangs alone on the right.

- **Don't** let a hero sticker cover the action row. The row is sized in px and the phone and the seal in lede ems, so their places carry a px floor and drop below the row on narrow windows; check any new placement at a narrow desktop (900x800) and a short laptop (1366x600) as well as the usual sizes.
- **Don't** show a sticker caption at rest; captions appear on hover or focus only (touch-only wide screens excepted).
- **Don't** reintroduce leader lines, hero stickers, sticker captions, the cursor preview, the cord, or clip marks under 860px. (The dust canvas and the icon stickers do stay on phones.)

- **Don't** add a second column, a sidebar, skill bars or meters, or any colour beyond navy, ink, metal, and white to the CV, and never let it run past one A4 page. Icons on the CV are the small navy contact icons only.
- **Don't** strike through before values or show change as struck-out text.
- **Don't** repeat a screenshot within one page.
- **Don't** title the last case study section "Next" or anything that reads as the next project; it is "What I'd do next".
- **Don't** add a floating table of contents, a hero banner, or a reading progress bar other than the cord.
- **Don't** tell booth kinds apart by colour; people, systems, and external services differ by form.
- **Don't** autoplay a demo with sound or under reduced motion.
- **Don't** show the "Reading" tag anywhere except the current index row on wide screens.

- **Don't** let the dust, the floating stickers, or the icon stickers carry meaning or copy: dust is canvas decoration only, a sticker still reads and links without its drift, and an icon sticker sits beside words, never replacing them.

- **Don't** drive sticker parallax or the float through `transform` on the slot; the slot's `transform` belongs to GSAP's entrance. Parallax goes through `translate` and the drift through the inner `float` span.

- **Don't** add icon stickers outside the closed set of eight, or print them in the CV; they appear only where the owner writes a `:name:` token in the statement or About copy, plus the fixed closing wave.

- **Don't** read the hero's ambient motion as a missing stop. The sticker float and the dust wander have no stop on the page: they rely on `prefers-reduced-motion`, which stills both fully, and the dust loop also stops while the hero is off screen. This is a deliberate exception to WCAG 2.2.2 for decorative motion, chosen by the owner (decision 2026-11-14), and changing it is the owner's call. If strict conformance is needed, the fallback is to let both settle a few seconds after load and after the last pointer move over the hero, keeping the pointer lean.
detectorExceptions: Nested cards: architecture booths are cards inside the twill field inside a stock page; the nesting is physical (objects on fabric on a sheet).
Display headings at line-height 1.0: page headlines and program index rows set line-height 1; running paragraphs never go under 1.45.
Per-project field colour on the next-project card: record data outside the palette tokens, contained to the field.

Marquee (achievements reel): the detector's marquee rule is ignored for mockup/index.html in .impeccable/config.json because the owner asked for this motion. For mockup/project.html the same ignore is a false positive: it loads the shared styles.css but has no reel element.
openIdeas: The closing panel could show the strap's other end, closing the loop the hero opens.
Seams could gain a fold edge (a thin shaded lip on the upper panel) so the join reads as sewn fabric rather than a dashed line alone.
narrative.pendingMigration: mockup/project.html and mockup/project.css still carry the single-ground structure: the page inherits the navy defaults as one flat panel without the twill, and its compact index bar keeps the ultramarine-era rgba(26, 39, 173, 0.94). To be migrated to the two-colourway world.
